chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn al-Sari, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man intends to marry a woman; can he examine her and look at her back and her face?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no harm in the man looking at the woman when he intends to marry her; he looks at her back and her face.'
ai.seo_question: Can a man look at a woman's back and face before marriage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly permits a suitor to inspect a prospective bride’s physical appearance, specifically her face and back, to ensure mutual attraction and compatibility before the marriage contract. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *mawaddah* (affection) and *rahmah* (mercy) as foundational elements of marriage, validating visual assessment as a legitimate step in the pre-nuptial process.
